title: A quantum oracle separation between QMA(2) and QMA
abstract: We find a quantum oracle relative to which $\mathsf{QMA} \neq \mathsf{QMA}(2)$. As a consequence, we resolve the no-disentanglers conjecture of Watrous: for every $ε+δ<1$, any $(ε,δ)$-disentangler requires input size exponential in the number of output qubits. Our proof combines the unitarily invariant polynomial method of She and Yuen (ITCS '23) with a new construction based on the symmetric and antisymmetric subspace projectors, reducing the $\mathsf{QMA}$ lower bound to the approximate degree of $\mathrm{OR}$.

bite.hook: We prove that QMA and QMA(2) are unequal by finding a quantum oracle separation.
tldr: They found a quantum oracle where QMA is not equal to QMA(2).
They combined the unitarily invariant polynomial method with symmetric and antisymmetric subspace projectors.
They resolved the no-disentanglers conjecture of Watrous, showing that disentanglers require exponential input size.
bite.whyItMatters: This resolves a major open question in quantum complexity theory regarding whether two proof systems are stronger than one.
bite.eli5: Imagine trying to check a puzzle with two helpers instead of one. For a long time, scientists weren't sure if two helpers could always solve tougher puzzles than a single helper. This research proves that yes, two helpers can actually do things one helper cannot.
